cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Integrated farm-to-retail model. BACKWARD: raw milk — the primary raw material — is sourced predominantly direct from farmers with no formal supply arrangements. As of March 31, 2026 the Company procured from 74,654 farmers (of whom 33,126 were women) across 25 districts of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Maharashtra, all within a 400 kilometre radius of Perundurai (67,615 farmers in Fiscal 2025; 67,807 in Fiscal 2024). Total raw milk procurement was 396.15, 307.20 and 272.80 million litres in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, of which 294.48 million litres (74.34%), 261.59 million litres (85.15%) and 263.55 million litres (96.61%) came directly from dairy farmers and 101.67 million litres (25.66%), 45.61 million litres (14.85%) and 9.25 million litres (3.39%) from third party dairy operators — the direct-from-farmer share has fallen sharply over the three years. Procurement is geographically concentrated in Tamil Nadu at 374.40 million litres (94.51%), 300.08 million litres (97.68%) and 271.77 million litres (99.62%); 'Others' (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh) was 21.75 million litres (5.49%), 7.12 million litres (2.32%) and 1.03 million litres (0.38%). Farmers are paid directly every 7 to 10 days, with middlemen eliminated; support includes cattle feed, silage training, fodder seeds, veterinary support, vaccinations, artificial insemination and cattle-loan facilitation, with 8, 10 and 28 farmer training programmes in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. A three-tier quality structure runs from 3,907 AMCUs (3 parameters) to 29 chilling centres comprising Milk Chilling Centres and Bulk Milk Coolers (21 parameters, located within a 30 to 40 kilometre radius of collection villages) to the Perundurai Manufacturing Facility (31 parameters). Realisation per litre of milk procured was approximately ₹77.79 in Fiscal 2026, stated to be the highest among listed peers (Source: 1Lattice Report). FORWARD: the Company operates its own logistics — as of March 31, 2026, 63 milk vans/tankers (average capacity 23,150 litres; 44 in Fiscal 2025 and 34 in Fiscal 2024), 282 reefer trucks with in-built refrigeration (payload approximately 10,485 kilograms; 252 in Fiscal 2025, 201 in Fiscal 2024) and 34 ambient trucks (payload approximately 24,350 kilograms; 21 in Fiscal 2025, 34 in Fiscal 2024), of which 26 owned vehicles are electric; IoT-enabled real-time fleet tracking and route optimisation, with return-load optimisation carrying third-party goods such as apples, cocoa powder, sweet corn, rice and butter. Stated to be the only dairy-focused company among its listed peers with entirely in-house logistics and manufacturing (Source: 1Lattice Report). Downstream cold chain at retail: 15,062 visi coolers, 25,824 ice cream freezers and 573 chocolate coolers deployed as of March 31, 2026, with a plan to deploy 30,000 ice cream freezers, 24,000 visi coolers and 12,000 chocolate coolers across Fiscals 2026, 2027 and 2028 funded partly from the Net Proceeds. Advertisement and business promotion expenses were ₹796.12 million (2.54% of revenue from operations), ₹711.32 million (3.03%) and ₹205.60 million (1.13%) in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. FURTHER FORWARD INTEGRATION PLANNED from the Net Proceeds: whey protein concentrate capacity of 10 tons per day and edible/pharma-grade lactose capacity of 44 tons per day (moving whey powder up the value chain from a bulk commodity), a dedicated 60 TPD yogurt plant with packing lines rated at 50,800 containers per hour, a fresh cheese line for feta and gouda, processed-cheese capacity addition with a continuous cooker, and a dedicated warehouse for cold and dry products within the Perundurai facility.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Any shutdown, breakdown, natural disaster, labour action, regulatory suspension or loss of the U.S. FDA/food-safety approvals at this single site would halt essentially all output, and the Company also flags under-utilisation risk (paneer capacity utilisation fell to 52.44% in FY2026 from 110.49% in FY2025 after capacity was raised from 72 to 192 MT per day).
- Raw milk is the primary input for every product; 94.51%, 97.68% and 99.62% of procurement in FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024 came from Tamil Nadu, sourced from individual farmers with whom there are no binding contracts. Price and availability swing with season, weather, cattle health and state policy, feeding directly into cost of goods sold.
- South India generated 69.23%, 71.00% and 73.68% of revenue from operations in FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024. Regional competitive, regulatory or climatic shocks would hit the majority of the revenue base, and the rest-of-India build-out is still early.
- Total borrowings of ₹16,718.53 million with a 3.61x debt-to-equity ratio as of March 31, 2026 (₹13,907.23 million fund-based outstanding as of May 31, 2026). Capital expenditure ran at 15.82% to 20.19% of revenue over FY2024-FY2026, one trademark is hypothecated to lenders, Promoter guarantees back certain facilities, and ₹4,968.61 million of the Net Proceeds is earmarked simply to deleverage.
- These three categories contributed 59.05%, 62.63% and 66.16% of revenue from operations in FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024. Failure to anticipate shifts in consumer taste, or a quality incident in any one of them, would disproportionately hit revenue.
- Shelf life ranges from 20 days to 12 months and products need chilled, ambient or frozen handling through an owned fleet. Spoilage, improper storage or transport, or a food-borne illness or allergen incident would trigger write-downs, product recalls, regulatory penalties and brand damage - the Company already faces FSSA proceedings over paneer samples in Ghaziabad.
- Working capital days were 48, 42 and 49 in FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024. The Company flags that failure to arrange adequate working capital, or inaccurate demand forecasting against short-shelf-life inventory, would adversely affect operations.
- Contingent liabilities aggregated ₹2,290.09 million as of March 31, 2026, of which ₹1,948.71 million is EPCG duty saved that becomes payable if export obligations are not met, plus ₹254.68 million of disputed statutory liabilities. Three indirect tax proceedings involving ₹313.91 million are outstanding, and the statutory auditors have included emphasis of matters and CARO/Rule 11(g) qualifications and adverse remarks for FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024.
